column3: “When the LORD took up” is rendered “was about to take up.”
“The life of your soul” is rendered “as you yourself live”; the oath form “if I will leave you” becomes “I will not leave you.”
“From over your head” is rendered “from over you,” and “also I know” as “Yes, I know.”
“From over your head” is rendered “from over you.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “on.”
“Hither and hither” is rendered “here and there.”
“A mouth of two” is rendered “a double portion.”
“You have made difficult to ask” is rendered “You have asked a hard thing,” and NASB adds “Nevertheless.”
NASB moves “also” to the second striking; the Hebrew “also he” may belong to the question. The meaning is uncertain.
“Sons of ability” is rendered “strong men,” and “lest” as “perhaps.”
“Turned behind him” is rendered “looked behind him”; NASB supplies “of their number.”
